items.h: A Review of the Winter Season's Final Events.
items.sum: Review of the end of the 1937-38 winter season: match v. Met. Police and Royal Navy, South of Thames, Southern and National cross country championships, and the Round Ilford and London to Brighton road relays.
e: South of Thames Cross Country Championship
items.s: A Review of the Winter Season's Final Events. Review of the end of the 1937-38 winter season: match v. Met. Police and Royal Navy, South of Thames, Southern and National cross country championships, and the Round Ilford and London to Brighton road relays. On Februray 5th we met the Metropolitan Police and the Royal Navy at Imber Court, over a six miles course. L. W. Herbert continued his good running by winning with Syd Ring and Jack Flower in the next two positions. Scoring 12 aside, the points were—Belgrave H. 151, R.N. & R.M. 274, Met. Police 394. The following week was the day of the South of Thames C.C. Championship, which was held at Cobham. We were not too optimistic, but hoped for the best, but with L. W. Herbert having knee trouble early in the race and falling right back, our team was eventually placed 7th out of an entry of 23 teams. Our scoring six and their positions were: G. Murdock 32, K. N. Wood 37, R. W. Tobin 45, R. G. Michael 50, R. W. Johnson 84, T. F. Morrell 106. February 26th was Southern Counties day at Ascot and the Junior race was first on the "card." Our team was placed 7th and as 23 teams competed, our juniors can be said to have done well. They finished as follows: E. H. Herbert 19, W. E. Beard 34, M. F. Edwards 43, R. Boyden 50. In the Senior race we suffered a disappointment in that we failed to win the title by the narrow margin of one point. The race was won and lost in the finishing straight, as Pat Parker lost two valuable places here. Our sixth man was also a little too far back to ensure success, but we were all pleased at the fine fight our boys had made. Our scoring six and individual positions are given: A. W. Penny 8, L. J. Cohen 13, C. T. Carter 16, J. Parker 19, H. W. Shields 23, H. G. Verney 37. Team scores resulted thus: Mitcham A.C. 115 pts., Belgrave H. 116 pts., Surrey A.C. 219, South London H. 221. 29 teams competed, and our team of twelve men won the "Odling-Smee" trophy awarded to the first Surrey club to finish a complete team; so that we can say that here was one honour that Mitcham did not win! "National" day at Reading, and after our fine show in the "Southern" we were at last hoping to "do" something. It was a very fast course, mainly grass land with no severe hills, and the weather being fine, the field swept along at a good pace, with Pat Parker up with the front bunch. Art Penny, and Les Cohen were also there with Tom Carter dogging their heels and after the first big lap things looked very rosy. The second time round, however, Les Cohen was seen to have fallen right back and eventually retired with stomach trouble, and Pat had also dropped from the leaders. Jack Holden, of Tipton, was now in front and barring accidents looked all over the winner. Never faltering he came round for the final lap and running in splendid style he recorded his first "National" triumph after 10 years of trying. Mitcham were also now in front of Birchfield in the team race and the four Welsh members of their scoring six all ran well to assist Thorogood and Brickwood in gaining team honours. We had dropped well back, but on the final scores being taken found that we had gained third place, due in the main to the forward running of our first three scoring men. Pat Parker is to be congratulated on his fine showing, which gained him another International vest. Our six and their placings were: J. Parker 7, A. W. Penny 13, C. T. Carter 18, S. T. Ring 50, H. W. Shields 52, D. Patience 59. The team scores resulted: Mitcham A.C. 91, Birchfield H. 116, Belgrave H. 199, Sutton H. 244, Salford H. 250, South London H. 313. On March 19th the "Round Ilford" Road Relay Race was held and as usual we entered two teams in this event. Charlie Smart went first for our "A" team and up against Palmer, the Southern champion, he ran extremely well to hand over about 30 yards behind the leader. Tom Carter went next and gave us the lead, which Jimmy Kemp lost, Cohen regained and L. W. Herbert kept, for Harry Verney to go away on his leg with about 150 yards over the Mitcham runner. Then came what was for us a serious misfortune, as Harry was wrongly directed at one of the turns; and by the time he had returned to the proper road the Mitcham man, who, strangely enough, had kept to the proper road, was in the lead. Shields set about his man in fine style and gained much ground, and then Ring took us into the lead once again. This was handed over to Bill Lucas, who was brought into the "A" team owing to Pat Parker's non-arrival. He had to give ground to Ivor Brown, who ran very strongly; and Brickwood, for Mitcham, went off well in front of Arthur Penny. The latter gained on his man slightly but was never near enough to threaten danger. We thus suffered another defeat to our close rivals, but in view of what happened we have every right to consider our team rather unlucky. May 7th was the day of the London to Brighton Relay race, which nowadays starts from Mitcham. The date was a very unsuitable one, coming as it did right at the start of the track season, and we hope the promoters will take steps to rectify this in future years. We had a very good team and with luck smiling on us for once we hoped to be the first team into Brighton, thus repeating our trio of wins in 1934/5/6. Tom Carter went first and in a very "hot" field handed over 6th. L. W. Herbert then went off and caught and passed two opponents, and then got on to the Mitcham man's shoulder. Then came disaster, for he was suddenly taken bad and could only manage to struggle along to hand over before collapsing. This left Harry Verney in 9th position but running like one possessed—Harry passed all but two of his rivals and handed over to Charlie Smart in 3rd place. His was a record-breaking effort, as it well deserved to be, and Charlie emulated his performance by doing record time over his course, although not gaining any places. Syd Ring went next and kept his position, and then Bill Lucas did likewise and gained slightly on the leaders. Actually, when he handed over to Arthur Penny we were 58 seconds behind. With a six miles stretch to traverse, we hoped to see Arthur doing "things", but he lost ground on Palmer and Bourton, the two leaders. Harry Shields plugged away on the 8th stage, and then Les Cohen went off in determined fashion and pulled back a little more ground. This left Pat Parker to do the final stage of just over 3 miles and it was seen that our hopes of catching either Mitcham or Birchfield were hopeless, Pat being 3 min. 19 secs. behind Brickwood, and 46 secs. behind J. T. Richards, who was reputed to be Birchfield's best man. Our man went off, however, in a "do-or-die" effort and simply eating up the ground, he ran until, to use his own words, "I caught sight of someone." Imagine our surprise when, after Brickwood had finished in comfortable fashion at the "Aquarium," we saw Pat coming along behind the Birchfield man. He was straining every effort to catch his rival, but the finishing post was too near, and Richards just lasted home by a bare 5 yards margin. Parker's time was a record for his stage and will remain for some time and it was certainly a great pity that Pat was not sent off nearer the leaders, as on his form anything may have been possible. Fortune has certainly not smiled on us this season, but with that typical "Belgrave" spirit I am sure our boys will make every effort to turn the tables on their conquerors when next season comes round. items.label: June 1938
items.sum: Report and full handicap result of the club five miles road race on 9th April, won by A. W. Penny in a course record; as printed, the 3rd and 5th starts (9 30, 9 45) and some handicap times and positions (e.g. Verney, Webb, Pritchard) do not agree with the other columns.
items.s: The Five Miles Road Race. Report and full handicap result of the club five miles road race on 9th April, won by A. W. Penny in a course record; as printed, the 3rd and 5th starts (9 30, 9 45) and some handicap times and positions (e.g. Verney, Webb, Pritchard) do not agree with the other columns. By "Ubiquitor." The 9th April was dull but not particularly cold and 27 starters went off at the usual fast pace. Parker, who last year acted as pace-maker from start to finish and won easily, was not amongst the starters, but J. C. Smart deputised very ably. When they reached the far corner, Smart led Cohen by a yard with Carter and Verney just behind, followed by Arthur Penny, Harry Shields, Jerman, Herbert, Ring, Taylor, Frank Webb and Lucas. The second lap took its toll, Smart being the first to crack and the "fast pack" became much more bunched in consequence. Arthur Penny had taken his training run position of pack leader with Tom Carter and Cohen on his shoulders. Smart ran behind with Verney, Ring and Herbert completing the bunch. Jerman was running exceedingly well just behind with Lucas 20 yards in the rear. Off the Common, past the Church and down the hill past the Hospital this pack slowly began to open, first one, then another falling back. Jerman was left first. Lucas, running an excellent race, about the same distance behind the leaders, passed first Jerman, then Harry Shields and Syd Ring. The leaders at this time were Penny, Verney, Cohen, Carter and Herbert. No change was made until well into Cambridge Road, when the tenth man had only about 100 yards to make up on the leaders, but here the pace—and distance—began to tell, and the leaders began to go away. Nevertheless, up the first half of the hill eight men were in sight (about 100 yards). Penny was leading with Herbert giving him the fright of his life on his shoulder. Verney was ten yards behind, and Carter and Cohen together another ten yards back. Back on the Common, Herbert was still going stride for stride with Penny, a magnificent performance. But along the far side Penny, being too old in experience for Herbert, piled on the pace till Herbert dropped back just before the Memorial, and when Penny turned into the home straight he had a lead of fifty yards, and won easily (although by only a narrow margin) in a really hard and gruelling race, the time constituting a new record for the course. Herbert, in following so hard on Penny, had shot his bolt and was beaten in by Verney, who held on tenaciously to the end. There were two items of great interest about the race: firstly, that the first 9 finished inside seventy seconds, which, in view of the excellent time, was a good omen for the "Brighton" on May 7th. Secondly, a tribute must be paid to the excellent work of the Hon. Handicapper, who not only got the first twenty in a few seconds, but produced no less than four "ties," one being for second place. items.label: June 1938
items.sum: Report of the triangular track match with London A.C. and 1st Bn. Worcestershire Regt. at the White City on May 4th, in which Belgrave finished second by one point.
items.s: Match v. London A.C. Report of the triangular track match with London A.C. and 1st Bn. Worcestershire Regt. at the White City on May 4th, in which Belgrave finished second by one point. On May 4th we visited the White City Stadium and engaged in a triangular match with the London A.C. and 1st Bn. Worcestershire Regt. We had a very enjoyable evening's sport and the final result was very close and very satisfying so far as we were concerned. In the 100 yards we only gained 1 point and that was by Stan. Blunden filling 4th place. A better result was seen in the 220 yards and with Tom Wiley being 2nd, and S. Lyons 3rd, we picked up 5 pts. here. The 440 yards saw S. Jarlett (perhaps better known as S. Garland, who has changed his name owing to family reasons) ran a very fine race to win this event for us. He fought off Borlase, of the L.A.C., in fine style and proved a surprise winner. Alby Bird was an easy winner of the 880 yards in what was rather slow time, but here we lacked a second runner and so lost a chance of picking up useful points. The 1 Mile saw the two Belgrave men, R. G. Michael and F. H. C. White, finish an easy 1st and 2nd, but this was rather discounted by the result of the 3 miles. Here J. F. Bain scored a victory for the L.A.C. by beating Arthur Allum, although the latter showed he is far from being a spent force. In the one field event F. E. Norman, a new member, showed useful form by clearing 20 ft. 11 ins. to finish second to Kiralfy of the L.A.C. The final points were: L.A.C. 29, Belgrave H. 28, Worcestershire Regt. 13, and considering the earliness of the season we were, as stated previously, very satisfied with the result. Stan. items.label: June 1938
items.sum: Report and results of the first club meeting of the season at Battersea Park on May 11th: the first Inter-Club Relay Shield contest, won by Belgrave from Mitcham, Croydon and Epsom, plus junior 220 yards, 2 miles walk and javelin handicaps.
items.s: Inter-Club Relays at Battersea Park. Report and results of the first club meeting of the season at Battersea Park on May 11th: the first Inter-Club Relay Shield contest, won by Belgrave from Mitcham, Croydon and Epsom, plus junior 220 yards, 2 miles walk and javelin handicaps. On May 11th we had the first club meeting of the season at Battersea Park Track. This was, incidentally, in a very bad state, due mainly to lack of attention and we trust that before the season is much older the L.C.C. will have taken steps to remedy the trouble. On the programme was the first of the series of four contests for the Inter-Club Relay Shield, of which we are the holders, and also three club handicaps. In the 4 x 100 yards we started, as we hope to finish, by winning this event, our runners being Tom Wiley, Les Bennett, F. W. Pritchard and Stan Blunden. The 4 x 880 yards came next and with Mitcham putting their best man first against Frank Webb, the latter did well to finish about 20 yards behind his opponent. Freddy White went next and, running in fine style, he easily overhauled his man and took us into the lead. Syd Jarlett strode round to keep our advantage and sent Alby Bird off with a winning margin, which the Mitcham man did not attempt to cut down. The 4 x 300 yards was another win for the "Bels" and here F. W. Pritchard, A. S. Blunden, T. D. Wiley and H. E. Pack proved much too strong for their rivals. Then came the final event, the 1 mile Team Race, and this proved the closest race of the evening. R. Thorogood, the A.A.A. 2 Mile Indoor Champion, was the individual winner, with Bill Lucas a good second. Then we had Dick Michael 4th, Harry Shields 5th, and Arthur Allum 9th. We won the team race by scoring 20 points to Micham's A.C.'s 22, a narrow margin but a winning one. The final points for the evening were: Belgrave H. 16, Mitcham A.C. 11, Croydon H. 6, Epsom H. 6. We had 10 entries for the Junior, under 19, 220 yards handicap and the winner proved to be R. Dunford, who made good use of his mark to beat G. H. Knight, with a newcomer in J. A. W. Scott in 3rd place. We have some very useful runners in our Junior ranks and with careful and regular training they should prove useful assets to our senior sides as they grow older. The Javelin Throw handicap was won by L. Jackson, who is our field events vice-captain. Ben May was second, with F. J. Skelley gaining third place on his first appearance in this class of event. In the 2 Miles Walk, Don Brown made a welcome return to form by winning off 75 yards. L. J. Coleman was second, with Joe Coleman third, so that it was in fact a back-markers' race. The whole field, however, were very close at the finish, and I am sure the Handicapper was satisfied at the result. items.s: Junior Match v. Poly. H. and Ponders End A.C. Report of the juniors' triangular match with Polytechnic H. and Ponders End A.C. at Paddington on May 12th, won by Belgrave. The Juniors paid a visit to Paddington Track on May 12th to take part in a triangular match with the Polytechnic H. and Ponders End A.C. In the 100 yards R. S. Turner gave us first blood by winning, and J. A. W. Scott was 3rd. Turner's time was the same as that of the senior race on the same programme, so that Roy must have felt well pleased with his effort. In the 880 yards N. C. Shrubb and F. S. Bradnum finished 2nd and 3rd, thus scoring more points for our team. Then R. B. Shepherd was 3rd in the 440, and in the final event, the 1 Mile Medley Relay, our team composed of L. Marchant, (880), N. C. Shrubb (440), J. A. W. Scott (220), R. S. Turner (220), finished an easy first; and the final points for the Junior match were: Belgrave H. 12, Poly. H. 7, Ponders End A.C. 5. items.h: Trophy Contest at Drayton Green Track.
items.sum: Report and results of the four-club contest for the new "Gordon Stewart" Trophy at Drayton Green on May 14th, won by Belgrave from Reading, Ealing and Ashcombe-St. George's.
items.s: Trophy Contest at Drayton Green Track. Report and results of the four-club contest for the new "Gordon Stewart" Trophy at Drayton Green on May 14th, won by Belgrave from Reading, Ealing and Ashcombe-St. George's. On May 14th we participated in a four-cornered contest for the "Gordon Stewart" Trophy, our opponents being the home club, Ealing Harriers, Reading A.C. and Ashcombe-St. George's A.C. In the 100 yards final Tom Wiley was placed second, and then in the 1 Mile Bill Lucas won in handsome style and, with Harry Shields gaining 3rd place and Tom Morrell 6th, all our runners in this race scored points to put us in the lead. The 880 yards was won by Alby Bird, with Dick Michael second. They had a ding-dong struggle which took them well away from their field. In the 220 yards final Stan Blunden finished 2nd, and we then had the 2 Miles team race in which our team was Alf Taylor 3rd, Art Allum 4th, and Dick Tobin 7th. This was not good enough to beat the Reading boys, who scored 1, 2 and 5. A. J. Hughes was the individual winner, his time being a shade over 10 minutes. For the final event, the 1 Mile Medley Relay, Bill Lucas sportingly turned out again to run the half-mile stage and he showed his fitness by giving us a winning lead. Eddie Pack did the quarter but did not extend himself, and the Ealing man gained slightly, but Les Bennett and Alec Mewes, our two sprinters, kept our lead to win a good race. The final points for the trophy—a very fine cup presented this year for the first time, and we thank the Ealing Harriers for giving us the opportunity of being the first holders of it—were: Belgrave H. 42, Reading A.C. 25, Ealing H. 22, Ashcombe-St. George's A.C. 13. items.h: Match v. Middlesex County and Poly. H.
items.sum: Report of the senior match with Polytechnic H. and Middlesex County A.A.A. and junior match with Poly. and Thames Valley at Battersea Park on May 21st, with S.A.A.L. events and club handicaps (senior match tied with Middlesex at 39 points).
items.s: Match v. Middlesex County and Poly. H. Report of the senior match with Polytechnic H. and Middlesex County A.A.A. and junior match with Poly. and Thames Valley at Battersea Park on May 21st, with S.A.A.L. events and club handicaps (senior match tied with Middlesex at 39 points). We had a very interesting meeting at Battersea Park on May 21st, when our visitors in a Senior match were the Polytechnic H., and a selected team representing the Middlesex County A.A.A. Our Juniors were also entertaining the junior teams from the Poly. Harriers and Thames Valley H. We started will in the senior match and Ted Gray caused a surprise by beating the R.A.F. runner, B.. Giles, in the 100 yards. The time was slow, due mainly to the rough track, but conditions were the same for everybody and our man is to be congratulated on his good running. In the 880 yards Alby Bird met his "bogey man," A. D. G. White, who was running for Middlesex; and once again Alby had to be content with second place. Brown walked well to beat E. A. Staker, with Percy Wright gaining third place. Eddie Pack ran for us in the 449 yards, and as befits the holder of the Middlesex County title, he won this event; with Syd Jarlett scoring a point for 4th place. A. V. Reeve showed a return to form in winning the 1 Mile for the Poly., but Bill Lucas ran a fine race in beating B. S. Cornish for second place. Then came the final event in the senior match, this being the 220 yards, and although Stan Blunden ran well to finish a close third we were unlucky in the fact that Ted Gray had to stop near the finishing post owing to straining a muscle. As results proved, another point gained in this race and we would have finished winners instead of tieing with Middlesex at 39 points all. The Junior match was composed of relay and team events and in the 4 x 110 yards the Poly boys were 1st, with our lads beating Thames Valley for second place. The 880 yards team race was won by Poly. with 13 pts., to T.V.H.'s 16, and Bel.'s 17. The individual winner was J. Bavage, of T.V.H., and L. Marchant and N. C. Shrubb ran well for us in being 3rd and 4th. Unfortunately F. S. Bradnum had an off-day in being 10th, otherwise we might have pushed the winners more. The 4 x 220 yards saw the first Thames Valley man give his team a winning lead and the Poly. beat us for second place. Our boys showed that they are badly in need of baton changing practice—a fault which is even displayed by international sides—but if our lads get together they should soon weld themselves into a useful combination. The senior match also included several field events and here our men did quite well, considering the strong opposition. In the Shot Putt our new member, L. J. Worrad, took 3rd place and in the Javelin Throw, C. A. Melchior gained a similar position for the club. Also on this programme we had two S.A.A.L. events and we made a good start towards regaining our place in the 1st division, from which we were relegated last season. In the 4 x 220 yards we finished second to the Victoria Park boys and here again faulty baton changing was noticeable. The 3 Miles Team resulted in a very easy win for our team, who finished: J. C. Smart (2), L. J. Cohen (3), S. T. Ring (4) and D. Patience (5). The only runner to beat them was R. F. Towndrow, of Ashcombe-St. Georges, who followed up his good performances over the country by displaying a fine turn of speed in this race. Thus from the two events we scored 11 points out of a possible 12, and a continuance of this form will keep us at the head of the table. There were two club handicaps at this meeting and in the 100 yards the winner of the final was F. J. Skelley, with F. E. Norman beating S. Lyons and thus reversing the heat form. F. W. Pritchard was unlucky in the fact that after qualifying for the final he had to participate in the S.A.A.L. relay which, owing to necessary alteration in the programme, immediately preceded the final. There was a good field for the 880 yards race, but unfortunately for them the race was a gift for the winner, W. T. Piggott, off 75 yards. He is a newcomer to the club ranks, but is a runner of much promise and we hope he will repeat this form, although off a much reduced mark. Alf Orton was second and here is a runner with possibilities, but at the moment his style is all against him, but it should not be too late for him to alter this defect. Dick Tobin kept among the prize-winners by gaining third place in a close finish; the field being well together, with the exception of the winner, who was out on his own. items.sum: Report of a match against Old Tiffinians A.C. and Old Emanuel A.C. on the Tiffin School ground, Kingston, on May 25th, won by Old Tiffinians with 43 pts. to Belgrave's 34.
items.s: Match v. Old Tiffinians A.C. Report of a match against Old Tiffinians A.C. and Old Emanuel A.C. on the Tiffin School ground, Kingston, on May 25th, won by Old Tiffinians with 43 pts. to Belgrave's 34. On May 25th we journeyed to Kingston to meet the Old Tiffinians A.C. and the Old Emanuel A.C. in a series of events on the Tiffin School ground. In the 100 yards we secured 2nd and 3rd places, through Les Bennett and J. C. Bright. The winner was Rampton, of the Old Tiffinians, a very promising sprinter. Les Bennett turned the tables on him in the 220 yards, and Bright was again 3rd. There was rather a surprise win in the 880 yards as Burnham, of the "Tiffs," dashed ahead at the bell and Harry Shields was unable to catch him. Alf Orton was third, but with the scoring 5, 3, 1, it will be seen that it was almost essential to have first places in order to keep ahead. The 440 yards found a similar result in that Baker scored a win for the home side; and we filled the minor places with N.C. Shrubb and D. E. Broom. The latter reminds one very much of J. C. Cooper Clark, who some of our older members will remember before he left us to go to Canada. In the 1 Mile the Old Tiffinians had D. G. Redstone, who is a really fine miler, and he won in easy fashion from Alf Taylor and Tommy Morrell. We scored a win in the Shot Putt, our Field Event Captain, Bill Sutton, doing 33ft. 10½in., which was too good for the opposition. Thus with three events to go the score was: Belgrave 27, Old Tiffinians 27, but as two of these were the High and Long Jump and, moreover, we had to field Frank Webb in the High Jump (in which he did well to gain third place) we were soon behind, as Charlie Jones could only get second place in the Long Jump. The last race was the 1 Mile Relay and with Redstone doing the half-mile stage, Harry Shields did well to finish about 10 yards down. Frank Webb did the 440—it really is astonishing how versatile Frank can be!—and then G. K. Talbot, and Stan Blunden ran the 220 stage, but at the finish we were still 5 yards behind the leaders. This made the final score: Old Tiffinians A.C. 43 pts., Belgrave H. 34 pts., Old Emanuel A.C. 4 pts. The latter side have only just re-formed and were weakly represented, although we were glad to see J. R. Shotter, who is a member of our own club, running for them. After the racing we had supper in the School, and so ended a very pleasant and enjoyable evening, for which we thank our hosts. items.sum: Report of the Evening Gazette Trophy contest at Palmer Park, Reading, which Belgrave won at the first attempt by half a point from Highgate, with a 10 miles road race and an S.A.A.L. relay on the same programme.
items.s: "Evening Gazette" Trophy Contest. Report of the Evening Gazette Trophy contest at Palmer Park, Reading, which Belgrave won at the first attempt by half a point from Highgate, with a 10 miles road race and an S.A.A.L. relay on the same programme. We competed in this contest for the first time, the venue being Palmer Park, Reading. The holders of the Shield were the Achilles Club and it was not with any high hopes of success that we made the journey. Owing to other fixtures clashing, we were deprived of the services of some of our best men, but so well did the others rise to the occasion that their absence was not seriously felt. The first trophy event was the 5 laps Steeplechase and in this Tom Carter ran a fine race to credit us with first place. His was also a very plucky effort, as he was badly "spiked" at the first water jump, and after the race he had to be taken to hospital to have the wound dressed. A. A. Robertson, the English International, chased Tom home, but he lost ground each lap at the water jump, which was a very stiff one. In the 880 yards Alby Bird easily qualified for the final, with MacCabe of the L.A.C., as also did A. D. G. White, of the T.V.H., and M. A. Melford, of the Achilles, and that old stalwart, M. Carr, of the Poly. The decider was a grand race; and after a hectic struggle MacCabe beat White by inches, with Bird about 5 yards away, third. The 440 yards saw S. Jarlett run well to qualify in the fastest heat; and he confirmed this running by being placed second in the final to his heat winner, W. H. Hammond, of Highgate. Then came the 1 Mile and the result of this race was the same as the previous Saturday at our own meeting. A. V. Reeve, of the Poly., once again beat Bill Lucas into second place, but as the time was 4 min. 25 sec., and Frank Close finished third, I think Lucas has every reason to be pleased at his fine running. Up to now the weather had kept fine after a very wet morning, but just as the Three-milers were getting to their marks it came down in torrents. There was also quite a wind blowing, and the runners were soon soaked to the skin. Charlie Smart adopted his usual forcing tactics and took the field along at a good pace. With a mile to go Furze, of the Poly, went ahead; with McIntyre, of Achilles, and Smart next, while H. R. Reid, of Surrey A.C. was also running very strongly. Over the last lap Furze had a winning lead; but Reid came through with a strong burst to gain second place. Harry Verney had also run a good race and was just beaten by an old team mate in Kibble, of Birchfield. Our third man was Syd Ring, who was quite a fair way back, but when they had totalled up the points the result was: Belgrave H. 33, Surrey A.C.35, Highgate H. 38 Thus it will be seen that we had scored points in nearly each event and so to our surprise we found ourselves well to the fore in the battle for the trophy. Ted Gray said he thought he would have a go in the Long Jump which took place in the pouring rain; and by doing 20ft. 2in. he tied for 4th place, and so gained what proved a most valuable half a point. Also on the programme was a 10 miles Road race in which Bert Footer made a welcome re-appearance and he led our team into second place in the team race. Bert was 4th man home in the individual race, which was won by R. P. Keay, of S.L.H. Herne Hill H. won the team race with 8 pts. as against our team's 13, whose actual positions were: H. E. Footer 4, F. A. Walker 5, and A. F. Mitchell 7. The S.A.A.L. 4 x 440 yards was also down for decision and we had to ask Jarlett and Gray to turn out once more for the Club, together with Dick Michael and Frank Webb. This meant that Syd Jarlett had done three 440's in one afternoon and Ted Gray had competed in the 100 yards, Long Jump, and then a 440 yards stage in the relay. Ted went first and gave us a lead which Frank Webb lost although fighting hard over a distance to which he is unaccustomed. Jarlett gained on his man, and then Michael got on to his opponent's shoulder only to be beaten down the finishing straight. The Victoria Park H. were the winners with ourselves second, Reading A.C. 3rd, and Ashcombe-St. Georges A.C. 4th. Ilford A.C. and North London H. did not start and it does seem as if the question of travelling in the lower divisions is a serious drawback. Personally, I think that if the divisions were geographically arranged with no question of 1st and 2nd Divisions etc., the league would be a better success than it is at the moment. After the racing all the athletes were entertained to Tea by the Reading A.C., and the Mayor presented the Shield and medals. Amidst loud cheering (and here our supporters made themselves heard!—we had two coaches to make the journey down) the result was given out: Belgrave H. 16½ pts., Highgate H. 16, London A.C. 14, Surrey 9, Achilles Club 8, Reading A.C. 7. We thus won the trophy at the first time of competing by the narrow margin of ½ point and to the Highgate boys we say better luck next time! items.s: Forthcoming Events. List of forthcoming track, relay and road fixtures from June 22nd to August 20th of interest to club members, with a plea against clashing fixture dates and the Running Hon. Sec.'s address for entries. We are now at the half-way stages of our Track season and so far results have been very encouraging; let us hope that we shall finish on the same high note. I append hereunder a list of events in which our club members will be interested, many of them actively. As regards our own club meetings at Battersea Park, I will not enumerate the events, as you should all have received your fixture cards and can refer to them for exact details. June 22nd (Wed.).—Battersea Park. Club meeting with 3 miles Track Championship for the "Griffin" Cup. Make a note of inviting your friends to take part in the two Novice races—100 Yards and 1 Mile run. June 25th (Sat.).—Chatham. Southern Senior Track and Field Event Championships. June 28th (Tues).—Richmond. We have a Junior match v. Thames Valley H., Poly H. and Thames Valley County School. June 29th (Wed.).—Charlton Park. Senior Match v. Cambridge Harriers. July 2nd (Sat.).—Eltham. Ravensbourne Meeting incl. 4 x 1 Mile "Victory" Relay and Open events. July 2nd (Sat.).—Southfields. As last year we are having an evening match with the Kensington Argyll A.C. and there is an 880 yards Handicap for our members. July 6th (Wed.).—Tooting. We have a Junior match v. Herne Hill H. and Mitcham A.C., also our seniors will engage Herne Hill in a field events match. July 7th (Thurs.).—Norbury. We have a "B" Team fixture with the London Assoc. Electric S.A. This should give some of those who do not run in the Inter-Club Relays a chance of representing the club. July 9th (Sat.).—White City. A.A.A. Junior Championships. Ponders End.—Open meeting incl. 3 Miles Team race and 1 Mile Relay, also Southern Counties 4 x 110 Yards. Woking.—Open meeting incl. 1. Mile Relay. Bexley Heath.—Open meeting incl. 1 Mile Handicap Relay. July 13th (Wed.).—Epsom.—Inter-Club Relays v. Croydon H., Epsom H. and Mitcham A.C. I hope our lads will turn up in full strength at this away fixture and so ensure success. July 15th and 16th.—White City. A.A.A. Championships. All members considered equal to gaining standard will be entered by the club and we hope to meet with even better success than last year. July 18th (Mon.).—Merton Park. We have a match with the Old Rutlishians, who have some very useful members in their ranks. July 20th (Wed.).—Battersea Park. We are entertaining the Milocarian A.C., of which A. W. Sweeney and D. O. Finlay are members. Also the Southgate H., who have some equally famous performers, in a series of match events. Our Juniors will also engage the Hercules A.C., Croydon H. and Mitcham A.C. July 21st (Thurs.).—Wimbledon Stadium. In connection with the Town's celebrations they have asked our club to put on some athletic events, and we have arranged for our members to compete in a 2 Miles race on this evening. There will also be a 1 Mile Relay and the novelty of competing at this venue, which is usually associated with the "dogs" and dirt track racing, should attract our members in large numbers. July 23rd (Sat.).—Birmingham. We are again making the journey to Perry Barr, the home of the famous Birchfield Harriers, to defend our half-share in the present ownership of the "Waddilove" Trophy. I hope we shall turn out an even stronger team than last year and so make our winning margin an undisputed one. Weadstone.—Kodak Meeting incl. 1 Mile Hcp. Relay. Cranleigh.—Open Meeting incl. 1 Mile Relay. July 27th (Wed.).—Mitcham. The final Inter-Club Relay meeting and I hope our supporters will come along to give our boys a shout. Knowledge of Welsh is not essential, although some of our boys wish they could speak it. Tooting.—On the same evening our Juniors are meeting the Hercules A.C. on another track in the same vicinity. July 30th (Sat.).—Tooting. The day of our Club Championships. We had to fix Tooting, owing to clashing of dates at Battersea, but in view of the deplorable condition of the latter track many of our members are viewing the change with pleasure. Study the club's time standards for each event and remember you never know what you can do until you are pushed to it. There are also standard medals awarded in the field events and Bill Sutton will be pleased to assist any intending entrants. Aug. 1st (Mon.)—Bank Holiday, and there are the usual crop of meetings but our members may be interested in the one at Chiswick which includes a 1 Mile Relay, also a 10 Miles Road Race, or at Oxted, where they have a 1 Mile Relay and a 7 Miles Road race. Aug. 6th. (Sat.).—White City. The City Police Meeting. I hope our members will keep Eddie Pack busy by giving him a bumper entry. They include a 2 Miles Relay at this meeting, which is on handicap lines. Aug. 10th (Wed.).—Battersea Park. Our final track meeting. I hope our members will turn out in good numbers for the season's wind-up. We are renewing the 300 Yards race—a distance which was once very popular with our members. Aug. 13th (Sat.).—Herne Hill. The B.W.S.A. Championships. These events are open to all who are members of Trade Unions, Leagues of Youth, etc., of which there must be many in our own club. There are events at all distances from 100 Yards to 1 Mile, 3 Miles and 10 Miles Run and 10 Miles Walk. Aug. 15th (Mon.).—Tooting. We have the last event in the S.A.A.L., Div. 2, this being the 1 Mile Medley Relay. I hope we shall not have too many members on holiday as this race may be the deciding factor in who goes up into the 1st Division. Aug. 20th (Sat.).—Imber Court. We have a match versus the Metropolitan Police A.C. and two other clubs are also joining in to oppose the very strong Police team. Motspur Park.—On the same day the A.A.A. 4 x 440 is being held at the Blackheath meeting, which includes Open events and a 3 Miles Team race. White City.—The Fire Brigade hold their annual meeting with the usual open events. I hope the above will prove of value to many club members. It may help them to make a note of these meetings in their diary and it is rather unfortunate that there are so many clashings on the same dates. This has been happening for many seasons past and surely it is time the governing body took steps to prevent such clashes, which are all to the athletes' detriment. A fixture meeting arranged early in the season would help clear the air so far as the various promoters are concerned. If any members would like further particulars relating to any of the above meetings, I shall be pleased to assist them. All entries for Club races to be sent to— E. A. DUFFETT, Running Hon. items.label: September 1938
items.sum: Editorial notes on a highly successful track season: newly married members, the engagement of coach F. Stampfl, the W. A. Rice Memorial Trophy subscribers, international selections, the AGM, subscriptions, honours badges, the Southern League setback and thanks to officials.
items.s: Editorial notes on a highly successful track season: newly married members, the engagement of coach F. Stampfl, the W. A. Rice Memorial Trophy subscribers, international selections, the AGM, subscriptions, honours badges, the Southern League setback and thanks to officials. The Track season, now completed, must surely be one of the most successful we have ever had. Our teams have won the "Reading Evening Gazette" Trophy and the "Waddilove Trophy," and in the "Kinnaird Trophy" Competition we made our best show to date. The "Doris" Shield and Inter-Club Relay Shield have fallen easily to us; and many of our members have been prominent in the important events of the Season. Perhaps the performance which gave us most pleasure was that of our team (Bird, Botwright, Jarlett, Pack) in taking second place to Achilles A.C. in the A.A.A. 4 x 440 yards Relay Championship. This was an excellent performance and an improving team may bring us our first A.A.A. team title next year. Gradually our track teams improve and in a year or two we may well be challenging for possession of the "Kinnaird Trophy." It is certain that in a complete athletic programme comprising all track and field events, Marathon and Walks with, say, two or three representatives in each event, we should be very prominent, and probably win such a competition if it were arranged. * * * * * Congratulations and very best wishes to our members who have taken unto themselves wives. They include : T. H. Scrimshaw, G. S. Doubleday, C. T. Carter, R. G. Hillier and J. Fletcher. * * * * * Members will remember that in these columns from time to time the question of a Coach to direct training has been raised; and we were forced to the conclusion that really capable coaches were very rare, and those that did exist were already fully committed. During the past months, however, we were fortunate in securing the services of a Continental coach, Herr F. Stampfl, whose vivacious enthusiasm and expert knowledge soon endeared him to our members. A fine all-round athlete himself, he is not content to tell others what to do, but gives personal demonstration and evidence of his own capabilities. Besides giving our track runners the outline of correct training, which should prove of great value to them in the future, immediate improvement was shown by some of our field-events men. Skelley and Melchoir, to mention two men, accomplished performances late in the season which two months earlier had seemed almost impossible. If it can possibly be arranged, we hope to have Stampfl's services during the Winter on the Field-event side; and for Track and Field events when the Track season re-opens next Spring. It cannot be definitely stated at this juncture if we shall have his assistance, but we hope we shall be able to continue in the same splendid way that was initiated this season. * * * * * The "W. A. Rice Memorial Trophy" subscription list has now been closed, and in due course a Cup will be presented to the Club for the Junior 880 yards Championship. This trophy will be a perpetual reminder of one who served the Club well in many capacities, and whose splendid qualities made him one of the most popular men the Club has known. Those who subscribed to this lasting symbol of appreciation of the friendship of one they were glad to have known were : J. B. Belchamber, L. G. Bennett, E. A. Duffett, F. H. Elson, E. Gordon, A. A. Harley, A. E. Harley, G. M. Murray, A. Patience, D. Patience, R. Patience, G. F. Pepper, G. H. Powell, C. W. Redgrave, W. Redgrave, T. H. Scrimshaw, H. W. Shields, A. E. Taylor, P. G. Wright. * * * * * Congratulations to F. E. Bentley upon his selection to represent Great Britain in the 50 kilos Walk at the European Games, and to C. F. Sutton upon being chosen as a reserve. Both Fred and Colin have well deserved these honours. * * * * * Congratulations also to Eddie Pack upon his selection to represent England at Dublin. Eddie has shown consistent form throughout the season, and he is unfortunate in having such a number of first-class quarter-milers contemporary with him. A few years ago Pack's times would have won A.A.A. titles. There can be little doubt that he was somewhat unfortunate in not receiving an invitation to go to the European Games, and when it was found that Bill Roberts could not accept, we should have thought that Pack would have been given preference over Horsfall (incidentally, an Australian). Pack's presence in Paris would also have strengthened the 4 x 400 metres relay team, which was beaten into second place by the German team. Pack in place of Barnes would, in our humble opinion, have represented a few yards improvement. However, we are not in the favoured position of the Selectors, and we can only hope that next season our man will secure his full share of honours. * * * * * The Club Annual General Meeting takes place at Belgrave Hall, Denmark Road, Wimbledon, on Tuesday, September 27th. It is hoped that all members will make an effort to attend, and take their part in the election of next year's Officers and Committee. * * * * * A few laggards have still to pay the current year's subscription, and our Hon. Treasurer would be glad to hear from them. Others, no doubt, will be anxious to be the first to pay their 1938/1939 subscription, which becomes due at the Annual General Meeting. * * * * * Congratulations to L. W. Herbert and J. C. Smart upon gaining their Club Honours Badges. Both succeeded in gaining A.A.A. Standard; Herbert in the Mile, and Smart in the 3 miles; and so qualified for the Club badge. * * * * * In a season that has given us so many successes, it is a matter for regret that we have been unable to regain our rightful place in the First Division of the Southern Amateur Athletic League. In the early races of the competition we scored heavily, but at the one mile team race only three of our runners materialised. and we were unable to start. This automatically robbed us of the leadership and our opportunity to regain First Division status. The presence of even one of our slower men would have enabled us to start in the Mile race, and some points would have been gained! An occasional setback of this nature is, we suppose, inevitable; but it is to be hoped that next year we shall not suffer in this way. * * * * * Now that the Track season is over, it is an opportune time to express our thanks to those officials who have made our meetings possible. Without running through the list of all who have helped, we must single out for special mention our old friend, Bill Fish, for his exceptional services to us all. A. G. Fell, always present as Starter, and A. C. Cook, our newly-found Announcer, have also helped considerably. items.sum: Walking notes: the A.A.A. Championships walk, Don Brown's illness, a 3 miles match win over Surrey Walking Club at Tooting Bec with full result, and prospects and notices for the road walking season; the printed result marks W. items.s: With The Walkers. Walking notes: the A.A.A. Championships walk, Don Brown's illness, a 3 miles match win over Surrey Walking Club at Tooting Bec with full result, and prospects and notices for the road walking season; the printed result marks W. G. True (11th) as Belgrave but counts his place in Surrey W.C.'s score. Our walkers made a brave show in the A.A.A. Championships. Cooper won once again, with E. A. Staker (Highgate H.) 2nd. Harry Churcher was third, Percy Wright fourth, and Don Brown and Joe Coleman also finished inside first-class standard time. Len Coleman was just outside, and we had five men in the first eight places. We had hoped that Don Brown would beat A. A. Cooper (as he had done twice earlier in the season, in the "Kinnaird" race and Inter-Counties Championships), but after winning the London Business Houses title ten days previously he was taken ill and confined to bed with a severe chill. The after-effects were obviously still upon Don in the A.A.A. Championship, and it was noticeable from the first ten yards that he was not himself. So severe were the effects of the chill that Brown did not race again on the track after the Championships. However, he has now started again for the road season, and we trust he will have more luck in avoiding chills next season, and claim an A.A.A. Championship. * * * * * On July 6th we were invited by Surrey Walking Club to meet them in a 3 miles race at Tooting Bec Track. J. G. Coleman and N. A. L. Burt, of S.W.C., had a spirited tussle, but Joe,s speed and strength prevailed and he led us to a win. Scoring six aside, final points were Belgrave H. 34 pts., Surrey W.C. 44pts. * * * * * The Road season is with us again, and there is no reason why it should not equal in success our last record season. Our training and racing programme is on similar lines to previous years, and over a number of years we seem to have arrived at a programme which gets our men fit, and fit at the right time, which is of the greatest importance. We are sure that given the keenness and perseverance which are so essential, we shall continue to do well. * * * * * We shall again have out all those men who have brought the Club honour and distinction in recent years. It is most important, however, that we also have some new recruits with the necessary qualities; and we trust all our members will be on the look-out for youngsters likely to embrace the sport. We have some very promising younger members, but there is always room for more. Remember that we hold a novice race early in the season! * * * * * Can we win the "Junior" two seasons in succession? An affirmative answer depends upon the keenness of the eligible men. Bridger, Heather, Thaxter, Roberts, Doubleday, Snell, and others, supporting Bert Clayton, our Eastleigh member, who may win the individual title, is certainly a team of possibilities. However, March is a long way off yet; and we shall have further opportunities of discussing this very intriguing question. * * * * * The Southern Committee of the Road Walking Association are holding their Annual Supper on Monday, November 21st, at the Empire Restaurant, Victoria. It is for men only and the charge is 4/-. We hope Belgrave will be well represented. * * * * * All members will shortly be in possession of their fixture lists, and any member requiring further information, or wishing to enter any of the races, etc., should write to the Walking Hon. items.label: September 1938
items.sum: Report of Belgrave's annual inter-club walking contests at Battersea Park Track on June 8th, with results of the four miles, three miles, two miles and mile races and the final points table won by Belgrave.
items.s: The Annual Inter-Club Walking Contests. Report of Belgrave's annual inter-club walking contests at Battersea Park Track on June 8th, with results of the four miles, three miles, two miles and mile races and the final points table won by Belgrave. Our annual fixture was held at Battersea Park Track on June 8th, and again we had a splendid evening's sport. As Woodford Green A.C. and Valentine's S.C. had their own meetings on, they were unable to send teams along; but we were glad to welcome Cambridge Harriers and Highgate Harriers for the first time for some years. The first race was held at four miles (reduced from the usual five miles) and we were represented by R. F. Elson and C. E. Churcher. Harold Whitlock (Met. W.C.) won from Neilson, of the Poly. Our walkers finished third and sixth and gave us a lead on points. Our score was 25 points, while Highgate H. and Polytechnic H. scored 23 points each. RESULT. 1, H. H. Whitlock (Met. W.C.), 30m. 49s.; 2, H. D. Neilson (Poly H.), 31m. 22s.; 3, R. F. Elson (Bel. H.), 32m. 16s.; 6, C. E. Churcher (Bel. H.), 32m. 59s. Belgrave H., 25 pts.; Highgate H., 23 pts.; Polytechnic H., 23 pts.; London Vidarians W.C., 16 pts.; S.W.C., 14 pts.; Cambridge H., 7 pts. In the Three Miles race, Harry Churcher quickly took the lead and won comfortably from our second string, Jack Rutland, who is destined to be of great use to teams in future years. This, of course, gave us the maximum number of points, Surrey Walking Club being the next best scoring club. RESULT. 1, H. G. Churcher (Bel. H.), 23m. 12s.; J. E. Rutland (Bel. H.), 23m. 43s.; P. J. Reading (Poly H.), 23m. 52s. Belgrave H., 31 pts.; S.W.C., 25 pts.; Highgate H., 17 pts.; Polytechnic H., 14 pts.; London Vidarians W.C., 13 pts.; Cambridge H., 11 pts.; Surrey Athletic Club, 11 pts. In the Two Miles race Don Brown and Percy Wright were our representatives. They finished in first and third positions, M. J. Fisher, the Banks Champion and S.W.C. man, taking second place. Again we scored heavily in the competition with 30 points, Surrey W.C. taking 27 points. RESULT. 1, D. E. Brown (Bel. H.), 14m. 59s.; 2, M. J. Fisher (S.W.C.), 15m. 15s; 3, P. G. Wright (Bel. H.), 15 m. 28s. Belgrave H., 30 pts.; S.W.C., 27 pts.; Metropolitan W.C., 22 pts.; Cambridge H., 21 pts.; London Vidarians W.C., 15 pts. The final race of the evening, the Mile, saw another Belgrave walker victorious. Joe Coleman had a terrific battle with E. A. Staker, of Highgate H., and eventually won by a yard in 6 min. 56 sec. E. A. Heather, our other walker, finished fifth and so once again we piled up points. RESULT. 1, J. G. Coleman (Bel. H.), 6m. 56s.; 2, E. A. Staker (High. H.), 6m. 57s.; 3, A. H. items.label: September 1938
items.sum: Report on the London to Brighton walk, won by Tom Richardson, in which a depleted Belgrave team finished third, Colin Sutton (eighth) taking the Club Long Distance Championship and Belgrave Cup.
items.s: The Brighton Walk. Report on the London to Brighton walk, won by Tom Richardson, in which a depleted Belgrave team finished third, Colin Sutton (eighth) taking the Club Long Distance Championship and Belgrave Cup. This year's classic found us poorly represented, and it was evident that our team would do well to take third place; and that we had not one chance in a million of retaining our hold on the Shield. Circumstances combined to weaken our entry. Fred Bentley was, of course, in France representing Great Britain at the European Games. Jack Bidgood found the pressure of work in a new position prevented him from training. Jock Martin, a stalwart for many years in this race, was indisposed, as was also Fred Rickards. Readman and Roberts were also prevented from entering and we could only muster six entries against last year's eleven. Our great hope was Colin Sutton. Unfortunately, a severe cold laid him low a week before the race, necessitating a day in bed, but Colin started in this race as though in perfect health. At 18 miles he held a good lead, but the effects of the cold began to show and he fell back. Pluckily he carried on, despite a very bad time lasting for some hours, and eventually finished eighth in 8 hr. 44 min. 52 sec. Bill Urry, as last year, gave a splendid show of even walking and finished tenth in 8 hr. 56 min. 58 sec. He was the first "Service" athlete to finish and, as last year, won the special prize. Our third man, in 18th position, was Harry Thaxter. He completed the course in 9 hr. 11 min. 7 sec., and so gained a first-class standard medal. Thaxter is young in walking experience and is to be congratulated upon an excellent performance. Our team was completed by E. L. Reeve, a Club-champion at shorter distances some years back. Reeve, together with Don Willis and G. S. Doubleday, finished inside ten hours and so qualify for second-class team medals. Doubleday improved an hour and a half over the previous year's performance, which was incidentally his first walking race. The race for first position was one of the most exciting and interesting seen on the road for many years. Henderson, after taking the lead from Sutton, went well ahead and it seemed impossible to catch him. He was pegged back, however, and the leadership was continually changing. Eventually Tom Richardson (Woodford Green A.C.) who had created new World's Records the previous week at various distances, including twelve hours, came through to win in 8 hr. 8 min. 1 sec. At Crawley he had been over 10 minutes behind the leader. Leicester Walking Club were worthy winners of the Team contest, with the promoters, Surrey Walking Club, second, and ourselves third. Of the 93 entrants, 89 started and 75 finished—an excellent record! All our six entrants finished, and Colin Sutton won the Club Long Distance Championship and Belgrave Cup. Second and third medals go to Urry and Thaxter. Next year we hope to give better support to the race and place a stronger team on the road. Our team on this occasion did well—no one can be said to have walked below form—but we have others who would strengthen our representation. Perhaps next year will see some of our younger walkers making their first efforts in this annual race—one of the finest of sporting events—and in the Club Championship held in conjunction. Once again we thank in all sincerity those cyclist attendants who helped our men along—a feat of endurance, patience and self-sacrifice in itself. A Club bus was on the road and supporters, walkers and attendants travelled back together, tired but eager to be on the road again next year. items.label: September 1938
items.sum: Light verse by W. H. Snell celebrating Belgrave's walking season and its walkers and officials, introduced by an Hon. Editor's note.
items.s: Well Walked! Light verse by W. H. Snell celebrating Belgrave's walking season and its walkers and officials, introduced by an Hon. Editor's note. [Hon. Editor's Note.—Bill Snell is the first member for some while to burst into verse in our columns, and whilst his metre sometimes falters, and occasionally the rhyme is suspect, we congratulate him upon the sincerity of his lay, and the trouble he has taken. We should like other members to polish up their iambic pentameters, their dactyls and spondees, and maybe we shall find a Belgrave Laureate]. Congratulations to all you Belgrave men, The Coleman Brothers, Joe and Len. In the "Junior" they dead-heated, A hundred others were defeated. Sutton and Reg Elson completed the team, Smashed all records—they stand supreme. In all the "Sevens" and Valentine's "Ten," First scratch team were Belgrave men. Harry Churcher is the the "Champ" of them all, Of the many champions from Belgrave Hall. Six consecutive "Opens" has this chap won, A marvellous performance, never previously done. They went to Colchester to walk mile after mile, Our men smashing records in amazing style. Then up to Birmingham to contest the "Twenty," Our chaps showing stamina that they had in plenty. We've often been second, or sometimes third, But this time it's ours—at last!—I heard. Filling positions two, four, eight, and nine, They've won the Shield—"Excellent! Fine!" Bentley, Sutton, Bidgood and Rickards, At distance-walking, you know they are wizards. The "50 Kilos" at Bradford we won, Completing a "season" that takes the "bun." And now all praise to A. A. Harley, And our Captain, good old Charlie. Hard work they've done behind the scenes, Selecting the teams—you know what that means! They must feel proud of the work they've done, After seeing the Cups their teams have won. To all you youngsters this sounds very nice, But to get to the "top" take Harley's advice. To all new walkers, we start in September, From Belgrave Hall (a place to remember!) You may now be slow, but plug away, Hard training will get YOU first one day. Down to Roehampton, or round the "Hills," Keep with the "pack,' road sense it instils. In future years, you've lots to do, To uphold our prestige, and we're looking to YOU! W. H. SNELL. items.sum: Review of Belgrave's field events season: a fourth consecutive Southern Amateur Athletic League win, club championship records, and a tied field events match with Herne Hill H. (two printed team totals, 63ft. 3in. and 278ft. 4in., do not match the individual marks as printed).
items.s: Field Events. Review of Belgrave's field events season: a fourth consecutive Southern Amateur Athletic League win, club championship records, and a tied field events match with Herne Hill H. (two printed team totals, 63ft. 3in. and 278ft. 4in., do not match the individual marks as printed). The season just finished has been the most successful ever in the Club's history. For the fourth consecutive year we have won the Southern Amateur Athletic League competition, scoring 243 points. This represents eleven points out of a possible twelve from each event in which we have competed. Charlie Melchior did well to win the Javelin event in the "Waddilove Trophy" Competition at Birmingham—our only win—and so contributed in no small way towards the winning of the Bowl. In match events, too, our field events men have scored more points than our opponents, so helping our match wins. Club Championships Day saw records go in the High Jump, Shot Putt and Long Jump. Pack had an easy win in the High Jump clearing 5ft. 5in., and Skelley's 22ft. 8in. in the Long Jump compares favourably with performances in International matches. If he maintains this form next year he should gain his place in our national teams. S. Jones had an excellent win in the Shot Putt with 39ft. 1in.—the best performance yet in Club events by "home" talent—only Grassau and Pfenninger having beaten it. L. J. Worrad is the new Discus champion. He has recently joined us and has already proved himself a great asset. He was also second in the Weight (37ft. 0in.) and narrowly beaten for third place in the Long Jump, with 19ft. 10in. H. M. Quackenbos is the new Javelin holder. Melchior and Powell were unable to throw, owing to the claims of work, but Quack's win is the reward of persistence. When he matures physically, he will throw 160ft. At the Blackheath H. meeting at Motspur Park on August 20th, Melchior was third in a Javelin handicap. His scratch throw was 166ft., his best yet. We congratulate S. Jones upon winning the Shot Putt event in the Surrey and Middlesex match on August 27th. S.A.A.L. RESULTS. We were first on 11 occasions, second four times, third three times, fourth four times. Fourth was the lowest position ever occupied. On July 6th we had a Field Events match v. Herne Hill H. at Tooting Bec Track. A most enjoyable match ended in a tie, each Club winning three events. We hope to arrange more fixtures of this nature next season. Our Field Events men were prominent in the match v. London Associated Electrical Undertakings. Sutton won the Shot Putt, T. C. Jones the Long Jump, and Quackenbos the High Jump. At Charlton Park v. Cambridge H. our men were first and third in the High Jump (Quackenbos and Marchant); first and fourth in the Discus (Sutton and Jackson); first and fourth in Javelin (Quackenbos and Jackson); and second and fourth in the Long Jump (Skelley and "Q"). Other good work was done against the Old Rutlishians at Merton; and v. Southgate H. at Battersea. We would again emphasise the welcome awaiting new recruits to the Field Events side. In particular, we should be glad of some more High and Long jumpers. So if you know of anyone, please inform :— W. H. items.label: September 1938
items.sum: Club notes on summer matches, the juniors, relay and team wins, members' individual successes, club quarters, overseas readers and H. Parker's election to the Southern Counties Cross-country Association committee.
items.s: This And That. Club notes on summer matches, the juniors, relay and team wins, members' individual successes, club quarters, overseas readers and H. Parker's election to the Southern Counties Cross-country Association committee. A very pleasant evening was spent at Southfields on July 2nd, when we met Kensington Argyll A.C. We had an easy win and outstanding recollections are of Alf. Orton winning the 880 yards handicap, our Walking Hon. Secretary winning the Mile Walk Match, and of Albert Smith running a "slow-motion" half-mile in the Relay, which we won. Certainly, a very pleasant evening. * * * * * On July 18th we visited Merton and opposed Old Rutlishians A.C., who won the match. We received a fine welcome, enjoyed ourselves immensely and hope for a renewal of the very attractive fixture next season. * * * * * A club "B" team visited Norbury on July 7th, to meet London Associated Electrical Undertakings. We managed to win most things; and we understand our Track Captain will long remember being passed in the last few yards of the Mile! * * * * * Our Juniors, both in numbers and quality, have been very prominent this year, and we are confident that there is much first-class talent here. On July 6th, at Tooting Bec, they scored a very impressive win over the Juniors of Herne Hill H. and Mitcham A.C. * * * * * Our teams excelled themselves at the Ponders End Fête and Gala when we won two trophies. Our Relay team (Bird, Blunden, Pritchard, Pack) win in fine style; and our lads in the Three Miles race (Smart, Cohen, Carter) gave us another team win. * * * * * Stan Botwright has shown improved speed this season and his wins include the Civil Service 220 yards title, two B.W.S.A. titles, two Club titles and a medal in our second A.A.A. 4 x 440 yards Relay team. He also won the invitation 440 yards at the City Police Meeting off 12 yards in fast time and showed that he is capable of extending our best quarter-milers. * * * * * We are very glad to see Bert Footer "on the the road" again, and successful at High Wycombe (2nd), Plymouth (1st), Chiswick (1st) and in the British Workers' 10 miles Championship. We hope he carries this return of form on to the country and gets his place in the International team once again. Charlie Smart has been one of our most improved runners on the track and, now that he is eligible, will probably go near winning one of our Cross-Country Championships. He should be of great help to our cross-country teams when eligible—next season. * * * * * While Eddie Pack was away in Scotland again winning the Police 440 yards Championship, Cadogan A.C. strove to retain the Middlesex Relay title. The handicap of Pack's absence was too great, however, and although the team ran well, Highgate Harriers won the title. * * * * * On June 29th we were at Charlton Park opposing Cambridge Harriers. The track was in good condition—probably the best of the L.C.C. tracks—and in a match comprising running and field events and a walk, we won fairly easily. * * * * * Our quarters at Wimbledon are now open on Saturdays, and the mid-week quarters at "The Rising Sun," Ebury Bridge Road, on Tuesday and Thursday evenings. We urge all members to make the fullest use of the facilities provided. On race days, in particular, we would ask all non-active members to come along to Wimbledon and help with the arrangements, if necessary. You are always very welcome, and we like to have with us those who no longer turn out themselves, but retain (as we hope all our older members do) a keen interest in the Club's activities. * * * * * We have a letter from W. J. Ashford, now in Iran, in which he asks to be remembered to all friends in the Club. Our Gazette goes to Singapore, to Iran, to Bert Button, one-time member, in New South Wales, to a pre-war member now in New York; and it would be interesting to hear of other "long-distance" readers. * * * * * We are glad to know that H. Parker, who has served as President of the South of the Thames Association during the current athletic year, has been elected to the Committee of the Southern Counties Cross-country Association. We are sure our representation is in very capable hands, and that Harry's many years of experience will prove an asset to the Association. Alf. Orton Alf. Orton won the 880 yards handicap v. items.sum: Look back at club happenings of 1928: a North v. South track match, the first Griffin Cup, inter-club walks, the club championship winners and Harry Hare's re-election as President.
items.s: Ten Years Back. Look back at club happenings of 1928: a North v. South track match, the first Griffin Cup, inter-club walks, the club championship winners and Harry Hare's re-election as President. It is of the utmost interest to glance at the "Belgravian" of ten years ago, to re-live those days, and to know of the happenings of 1928! A track match was held between those living North of the Thames and those residing south of the river. Duffett managed the "South" team and Harley the "North" team, and an interesting match was won by the "North" by 4 events to 3. Among the Juniors running were T. H. Scrimshaw, T. C. Jones and T. F. Morrell. The Two Miles race was won by Bill Webb (N) narrowly from Bill Rice (S). All races were on team and relay principle and gave rise to great interest, and the present existence of Cadogan A.C. may be said to owe something to this meeting. The first Club championship for the "Griffin" Cup was held, and won by Jack Flower in 15 min. 21 sec. Duffett was second, and Micky Pyer third. At the same meeting Scrimshaw easily won an 880 yards handicap, off 40 yards, showing some of the form which was later to earn him International honours. The Inter-Club Scratch Walks of 1928 were won by Belgrave with 77 points; Ashcombe A.C. taking second place with 64 points. The Club Championships were won as follows: 100 yards, M. E. Odell (10.4 sec.); 440 yards, J. Cooper Clark (51 sec.); 880 yards, J. Cooper Clark (2 min. 1.6 sec.); Mile, T. J. Flower (4 m. 39.8 sec.); 2 miles Walk, R. D. McMullen (15 min. 4.4 sec.); 220 yards Junior, J. A. Ford (24.2 sec.). Some handicaps were included in the programme and were won as follows: 75 yards, E. Gordon; 880 yards, H. L. Rollins; 220 yards, Hurdles, T. C. Jones. It is noted that W. G. Webb won the "Fire Brigade" Mile, and at this time the identity of "Observer," who contributed notes regularly, was the cause of much enquiry and discussion. At the A.G.M. held in September, 1928, Harry Hare, who has served the Club in practically every capacity and also found time to score in Championship winning teams, was re-elected as President of the Club. These were the happenings of ten years ago! Duffett Duffett 1928: managed the "South" team; 2nd in first "Griffin" Cup championship Harley Harley 1928: managed the "North" team T. H. Scrimshaw T. H. items.sum: Notice of the 1938-39 social programme: two dances at the Ball Room, Zeeta House, Putney Hill, socials at Wimbledon, a Boxing Day Party and the Club Dinner fixed for May 7th, 1939 at The Empire Restaurant, Victoria.
items.s: Our Social Programme. Notice of the 1938-39 social programme: two dances at the Ball Room, Zeeta House, Putney Hill, socials at Wimbledon, a Boxing Day Party and the Club Dinner fixed for May 7th, 1939 at The Empire Restaurant, Victoria. Two Dances have been arranged to take place at The Ball Room, Zeeta House, Putney Hill, during the coming season. They are to be held on November 26th, 1938, and February 11th, 1939, and we have no doubt that our members will enjoy themselves at this newly-built hall. Situated at the junction of Putney Hill and Lower Richmond Road, almost on top of Putney Station (Southern Rly.) and served by many bus routes, our members should find it extremely easy of access. Socials at Wimbledon will be held on October 1st, October 22nd, December 10th, January 28th, and March 25th; and, in addition, we shall hold a Boxing Day Party, as last year. For the benefit of those who are marking up their 1939 diaries, the Club Dinner has been fixed for May 7th and will be held at The Empire Restaurant, Victoria. items.label: September 1938
items.sum: Report on the 1938 Inter-Club Relay Shield contests against Mitcham A.C., Epsom H. and Croydon H., which Belgrave won again with 63 points out of a possible 64.
items.s: The “Inter-Club” Relay Shield Contests. Report on the 1938 Inter-Club Relay Shield contests against Mitcham A.C., Epsom H. and Croydon H., which Belgrave won again with 63 points out of a possible 64. The second in this series was held at Croydon on May 31st, and we fielded quite a strong team and dropped only 1 point out of a possible 16. We won both the 4 x 100 yards and 4 x 300 yards relays, and then after a close and exciting race we also won the 4 x 880 yards. We were not so strongly represented in the 1 Mile team race, and Mitcham proved the winners of this with Bob Thorogood as the individual winner. The points scored that evening were : Belgrave H. 15, Mitcham A.C. 12, Croydon H 8, Epsom H. 5. On 13th July we visited Epsom for the third contest and once again the “turn-out” of our chaps was good to see. Unfortunately the same could not be said for our opponents and Mitcham were very weakly represented. The racing was more or less a procession, with our boys in front, and we won all four events. The points scored were : Belgrave H. 16, Mitcham A.C. 11, Epsom H. 7, Croydon H. 6. The final meeting was held at Mitcham on July 27th, and here again we scored maximum points in winning the four events down for decision. It was a pity that Mitcham did not put up a better fight on their own track, and they really have seemed very apathetic over the season’s contests. As regards Croydon and Epsom, we appreciate the hard fight they have in fielding teams; but from a club of Mitcham’s strength and reputation we expect keen opposition. If they cannot do better than this I am very much afraid their period of triumphs is nearing the end. We once again won the Shield, the final points being : Belgrave H. 63, Mitcham A.C. 46, Epsom H. 24, Croydon H. 20. As the highest possible is a total of 64 it will be seen we dropped only one point throughout the series of contests, a record which will stand for many years, and for which our boys deserve every congratulation. They rallied round in fine style and it was a great pity that our rivals did not take these contests in the same spirit. I trust that next season will see the same fine exciting battles that we have previously had for the possession of the Shield. Bob Thorogood Bob Thorogood individual winner of the 1 Mile team race, Croydon, May 31st Inter-Club Relay Shield Croydon Epsom Mitcham Mitcham A.C. Croydon H. Epsom H.

items.label: September 1938
items.sum: Report on the “Doris” Shield contest at Battersea Park Track on June 15th, won by Belgrave from Ashcombe-St. George's A.C. and Thames Valley Harriers despite a track in very bad condition. Handicap results for the 100 yards, 2 miles walk and 1 mile follow.
items.s: The “Doris” Shield Contest. Report on the “Doris” Shield contest at Battersea Park Track on June 15th, won by Belgrave from Ashcombe-St. George's A.C. and Thames Valley Harriers despite a track in very bad condition. Handicap results for the 100 yards, 2 miles walk and 1 mile follow. This season’s meeting was held at Battersea Park Track on June 15th and, as usual, the track was in a very bad condition. In fact, some of the athletes considered it dangerous to run on, and abstained from competing, which is to be regretted; and when things come to such a pitch as this it is high time the L.C.C. were asked to take this question in hand. The holders of the trophy were the Thames Valley Harriers and after making a very bad start in the 100 yards scratch race, they more or less gave up heart and did not compete in the final event. They took this stand on the condition of the track, and A. D. G. White, the Scottish International runner, was one of their members who refused to run. A. T. Liffen, of Ashcombe-St. George’s, won the 100 yards, with Stan Botwright and Tom Wiley filling the next two places. With the points scoring 6 down to 1 in each event, we thus got away to a flying start with 9 points from the first race. In the 440 yards Eddie Pack refused to risk a breakdown owing to the loose surface; and for an athlete of his build his point of view can be readily understood. Dick Michael made a fine substitute, however, and he ran well to beat Flynn of T.V.H., while Frank Webb sportingly turned out and gained points by finishing 4th. The 2 Miles Team race resulted in an easy win for our team and they actually finished abreast in first position. Our three were : Les Cohen, Tom Carter and Charlie Smart, and their time of 9 min. 56 sec. was very good, bearing in mind the state of the track. For the final event, the 1 Mile Relay, Thames Valley H. did not field a team, and we won after a good race with Ashcombe-St. George’s A.C. The final points for the Shield were : Belgrave H. 30, Ashcombe-St. George’s A.C. 21, Thames Valley H. 12. As usual at this meeting, we had three handicap events open to members of the competing clubs. In the 100 yards there were many absentees and with one heat a walk-over, and some of the others with two or three runners only, we had a final of 5 runners—all “Bels.” F. W. Pritchard (5) won a good race with R. B. Shepherd (8) second, and S. Lyons (4) third in 10.3 secs. The 2 Miles Walk proved another good race and a promising young walker in A. E. Elliott (475) was the winner with S. Mable (575) second, and W. True (550) third. These are all long-markers but the rest of the field was very close up. A good field was seen out in the 1 Mile handicap, and here a visitor in W. F. Gant, of T.V.H., off 130 yards, ran a well-judged race to run home a good winner. R. W. Tobin, of Belgrave, off 100, was second and Bert Cook, better known as a Poly Harrier, was third off 110 yards. A. D. G. White A. D. G. items.label: September 1938
items.sum: Report on the Kinnaird Trophy meeting at the Polytechnic Harriers' new ground at Chiswick, won by Achilles with Belgrave fifth on 12 points, with Tom Carter second in the Southern Counties 2 Miles Steeplechase, a Belgrave team win in the Invitation 2 Miles Walk and Belgrave finishers in the Marathon.
items.s: The “Kinnaird Trophy” Meeting. Report on the Kinnaird Trophy meeting at the Polytechnic Harriers' new ground at Chiswick, won by Achilles with Belgrave fifth on 12 points, with Tom Carter second in the Southern Counties 2 Miles Steeplechase, a Belgrave team win in the Invitation 2 Miles Walk and Belgrave finishers in the Marathon. We were once again honoured by receiving an invitation to compete at this meeting, which was held at the fine new ground of the Polytechnic Harriers at Chiswick. As usual our boys gave a very creditable display in being placed fifth in the list of competing clubs which included all of any note. Achilles, with their formidable list of talent to draw on—far in excess of any that an ordinary club can command—were easy winners of the trophy with a total of 71 points. Highlights of the meeting so far as we were concerned were Stan Botwright’s fine running in the 220 yards, and in his heat he caused a surprise by beating J. C. Horsfall, of Achilles Club. In the final he was placed 4th, and so scored 3 points. Another fine performance was Eddie Pack’s running in the 440 yards, and after an easy heat win, he made A. G. K. Brown go all the way in the final. Eddie was leading at 300 yards, but once the straight was reached Brown forged ahead, and Eddie was also “pipped” on the tape for second place by C. H. Kearney, the American running for Achilles. It was one of Pack’s best runs to date and if he could only find something of a finish, I would back him against the best in the country. In the 880 yards Alby Bird ran his usual consistent race and although coming up against his “bogey” man, A. D. G. White, in his heat they both managed to qualify for the final. This was a fine race and White proved the winner, just beating J. V. Powell, with Bird in third place. These three runners had so far scored 11 points for us, which was in excess of any number scored previously by us in these contests, and then Charlie Smart, by gaining 6th place in the 3 Miles, brought our totai to 12. At this meeting was held the Southern Counties 2 Miles Steeplechase and although the water jump was far from satisfactory, after some discussion it was decided to hold the race. Tom Carter put up very good and plucky show and after Abberton, of Q.P.H.—he is also a member of the “Bels”—had led most of the way Tom looked like making up the lost ground with a lap to go. Then, bad luck, Tom hit a hurdle and fell and although still retaining second place, he found it impossible to catch the leader. In the Invitation 2 Miles Walk, the Belgrave boys gave the fair sized crowd a good example of the heel and toe “stuff” and Don Brown walked in his best style to beat A. A. Cooper, the A.A.A. champion. Joe Coleman was third, and with Harry Churcher, Percy Wright, Len Coleman and J. E. Rutland giving good support, we scored an easy win in the team race by scoring 13 pts. to Surrey Walking Club’s 39, four aside scoring. In the Marathon, F. A. Walker and A. F. Mitchell ran well to gain first class standards; and Bert Lindsey and F. G. White finished the course and completed our team. Stan Botwright Stan Botwright 4th, 220 yards final (3 points); beat J. C.
